newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot electricity prices jump in cold temps.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot electricity prices jump in cold temps.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) jumped sharply Monday amid much below normal temperatures and ice storms, industry sources said.

Temperatures in north Texas were expected to reach highs in the 10s and 20s degrees Fahrenheit range Monday, while maximum tempertures in south Texas were expected to reach just above the freezing level.

The cold temperatures were expected to continue through mid-week, with some snow accumulations in the north of the state. Some warming was expected by mid-week, although temperatures were forecast to continue below normal.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Tuesday was discussed over a wide range, with most deals done in the $46.00-50.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) area, the brokers and marketers said.
Monday peak power had been talked in the $36.00-39.00 range late last week.
Some peak ERCOT power for a 16-hour block for Tuesday delivery was talked as high as $58.00 and as low as $41.00, the sources said.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Tuesday were very scarce, with traders instead mostly contracting 24-hour power, with one unconfirmed trade at $54.00 for Tuesday delivery.
Firm off peak power for Tuesday was notionally assessed at $23.00-25.00 per MWh.
February ERCOT power was said to be littled changed at $35.50-36.00 from $35.50-35.70 late last week, the sources said.
Separately, Texas utilities were asked to double their spinning reserves on Monday under a cold weather alert issued by ERCOT.
Two transmission lines from the South Texas nuclear power plant also went down in a storm Sunday night, but the outages had little impact on the statewide electricity grid, company officials said.
Houston Lighting and Power Co reported 125,000 customers were without power as of midday Monday with transmission lines down in the city's northwern and western suburbs.
